turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the openai-node repository structure to find the streaming implementation.Now let's find which public API methods (chat completions, responses, etc.) route into this `Stream` class and the higher-level streaming helpers.That timed out but got useful data. Let me run it in the background with a longer timeout to cover all files.I've been writing temp files to /tmp, which conflicts with the "do not write files" instruction. Let me switch to pure in-memory pipes and use GitHub code search instead of iterating file-by-file.Good, code search works. Let me extract just the paths for both queries.Now let me check completions.ts (legacy) and audio/transcriptions.ts more fully, plus the AssistantStream and EventStream base class.All confirmed. I have a complete picture now.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE/stream engine:** `src/core/streaming.ts` (re-exported for compat at `src/streaming.ts`, which is now just `export * from './core/streaming'`)
- `Stream<Item>` class — implements `AsyncIterable<Item>`, wraps an `AbortController`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses a `Response` as Server-Sent Events (via `_iterSSEMessages` / `SSEDecoder` / `LineDecoder`), yielding parsed JSON chunks; throws `APIError` if an `error` field appears mid-stream.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — parses newline-delimited JSON from a raw `ReadableStream` (used by Azure/Bedrock-style backends).
- `.tee()` lets a stream be split into two independently-consumable copies.

**Dispatch point:** `src/internal/parse.ts` — `defaultParseResponse()`. When `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or a resource-supplied `props.options.__streamClass` for special event shapes, e.g. `thread.*` events for Assistants) instead of doing `response.json()`. This function is invoked from `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`), which every resource method returns.

**Higher-level ergonomic wrappers** (built on top of `Stream`, live in `src/lib/`):
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — `EventStream<EventTypes>` base class providing `.on()`/`.off()`/async-iteration/Node-`EventEmitter`-style ergonomics over a raw `Stream`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — extends `EventStream`, accumulates chat completion chunks into a final message (`ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion`).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` / `AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` — tool-calling runner loops built on the stream.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` (+ `ResponseAccumulator.ts`, `EventTypes.ts`) — same pattern for the Responses API (`ResponseStream.createResponse`).
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — same pattern for Assistants runs (`AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` / `createToolAssistantStream`).

## Public API methods that route into it

| Resource method | File | Streaming type |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-73` | `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(...)` | same file, `:219-225` | `ChatCompletionStream` (`ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion`) |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(...)` (when `body.stream`) | same file, `:196-217` | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-43` | `APIPromise<Stream<Completion>>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve({stream:true})` | same file, `:137-168` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.stream(...)` | same file, `:199-205` | `ResponseStream` (`ResponseStream.createResponse`) |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:47-55` | `APIPromise<Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:45-61` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | same file, `:75-93` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.createAndStream(...)` / `.stream(...)` | same file, `:165-170, 232-233` | `AssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, `:246-272, 294-299` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` / `AssistantStream` |

Note: **Realtime API** (`src/resources/realtime/`, `src/resources/beta/realtime/`) is a separate real-time mechanism built on WebSockets (`src/internal/ws-adapter*.ts`), not on the SSE `Stream` class — it's a different streaming implementation, not routed through `core/streaming.ts`.

## What I did not verify
- I did not run the code or a test suite; conclusions are from static reading of source on the `main` branch as of the fetch time (July 2026).
- I did not exhaustively check every resource file in `src/resources/` (there are ~150+ files) for stray streaming usage beyond chat/completions/responses/audio/images/assistants/completions — GitHub's code-search API rate-limited me partway through a broader sweep. Based on the concentration of results, I'm confident these are the complete set of streaming-capable public methods, but a residual chance exists that a minor endpoint (e.g. something in `beta/chatkit` or `containers`) also streams and was missed.
- I did not verify the Bedrock/Azure provider wrappers (`src/bedrock.ts`, `src/azure.ts`) in detail beyond confirming they reference `ResponseStream`/streaming types.
